blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how does your body work?
blocks.say: Today we explore how your body works. Bones, muscles, teeth, food and the heart all have jobs.

blocks.alt: A model skeleton with its hand under its chin
blocks.caption: A model of the human skeleton.
blocks.credit: Photo by Mathew Schwartz on Unsplash
blocks.say: This model shows a skeleton. Under your skin, bones hold you up and protect your soft organs.

blocks.markdown:
The **skeleton** supports, protects and helps us move.

The skull protects the brain. The ribs protect the heart and lungs.
blocks.say: Under your skin is a framework of bones called your skeleton. An adult has 206 bones. The skeleton does three jobs. It supports your body so you can stand up. It protects soft organs. Your skull protects your brain, and your ribs protect your heart and lungs. And it helps you move, together with your muscles. Look at the bones inside the body.

scenes.caption: Bones support the body.
scenes.say: Here is a body. Its bones form the skeleton. The bones hold the body up.

scenes.caption: Bones protect soft organs.
scenes.say: The skull is a hard box that protects the soft brain. The ribs make a cage around the heart and lungs.

blocks.alt: A model of a spine and rib cage on a grey background
blocks.caption: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs.
blocks.credit: Photo by Nino Liverani on Unsplash
blocks.say: Look at the rib cage. It is a bone cage that protects the heart and lungs.

blocks.markdown:
**Muscles** pull on bones to make them move. They work in pairs.

A **joint**, like the elbow, is where two bones meet and can bend.
blocks.say: Bones cannot move on their own. Muscles move them. A muscle can only pull, never push, so muscles work in pairs. To bend your arm, the biceps muscle on top gets shorter and pulls. To straighten it, the triceps underneath pulls the other way. Tendons join muscles to bones, and joints, like your elbow, let the bones bend.

scenes.caption: Biceps pulls: the arm bends.
scenes.say: To bend the arm, the biceps on top pulls and gets shorter. The triceps relaxes.

scenes.caption: Triceps pulls: the arm straightens.
scenes.say: To straighten the arm, the triceps pulls and the biceps relaxes. A muscle can only pull, so it needs a partner.

question.hint: That is why they work in pairs.
question.explanation: Muscles can only pull, so they work in pairs to move bones in two directions.

blocks.title: A day inside Fatima's body
blocks.transcript: Fatima bites an apple. Her sharp front teeth cut it. Her flat back teeth grind the food. Saliva makes it soft to swallow. The food slides down the oesophagus. The stomach churns it with acid. In the small intestine, nutrients pass into the blood. Waste goes on. Fatima jumps rope. Her muscles pull her bones, and they work in pairs. Her heart beats faster. It pumps more oxygen to her working muscles. At night she brushes her teeth. That stops sugar turning into acid. Bones, muscles, teeth and a heart all work together. Well done, Fatima!
blocks.caption: Follow a snack and a jump through Fatima's body.

blocks.text: Stop 1: A journey through the body

blocks.markdown:
**Digestion** breaks food into tiny pieces your body can use.

Food travels through the mouth, oesophagus, stomach and intestines.
blocks.say: Digestion is how your body breaks food down so it can use it. It starts in your mouth. Your teeth chew the food, and saliva makes it soft. You swallow, and the food moves down the oesophagus to the stomach. There, strong acid and churning muscles turn it into a thick liquid. Then it moves into the small intestine. Watch a meal make its journey.

scenes.caption: Mouth: chewing.
scenes.say: In the mouth, teeth chew the food and saliva starts to break it down.

scenes.caption: Stomach: churning.
scenes.say: The stomach churns the food with acid. It becomes a thick liquid.

scenes.caption: Intestines: nutrients absorbed.
scenes.say: In the small intestine, nutrients pass into the blood. The large intestine takes out water, and the waste leaves the body.

question.prompt: Put the food's journey in order.
question.explanation: Food goes from the mouth down the oesophagus to the stomach and then the small intestine.

blocks.title: Digestion jobs
blocks.goal: Put each job in the right place: Breaks food down or Takes in nutrients.
blocks.say: You can show digestion with a model. Put a banana and a little water in a strong bag. Squash it with your hands. That is the stomach churning. Squeeze the mush into a tight sock or tights, and see the liquid come out. That is what the small intestine does with nutrients. Then try matching the parts to jobs.

blocks.markdown:
**Incisors** cut, **canines** tear and **molars** grind.

Adults have 32 teeth.
blocks.say: You have different teeth for different jobs. Incisors at the front are sharp and cut food, like biting an apple. Canines are pointed and tear food. Molars at the back are flat and grind food. Children have twenty milk teeth, and adults have thirty-two. Look at the three kinds.

question.explanation: Molars are flat and grind food.

blocks.markdown: Brush twice a day with **fluoride** toothpaste, eat less sugar and visit the dentist.
blocks.say: Sugar is bad for teeth. Bacteria in your mouth feed on sugar and make acid, which wears away the tooth. This is tooth decay. To protect your teeth, brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, limit sugary snacks, and visit the dentist. Many Muslims also use a miswak. The Prophet, peace be upon him, encouraged keeping the teeth clean.

blocks.markdown:
The **heart** pumps **blood** around the body.

Your **pulse** is how many times your heart beats.
blocks.say: Your heart is a muscle that pumps blood all around your body. Blood carries oxygen from the lungs, and nutrients from food, to every part. It also carries waste away. You can feel your heartbeat as a pulse in your wrist. When you exercise, your muscles need more oxygen, so your heart beats faster. Let's look at the heart.

blocks.alt: Soap, covering a sneeze and a vaccine help stop germs.
blocks.caption: Soap, covering a sneeze and a vaccine help stop germs.
blocks.say: Germs are tiny living things, like bacteria and viruses, that can make us ill. They spread through coughs, sneezes and dirty hands. We stop them by washing hands with soap, covering coughs, and keeping clean. A hadith teaches that cleanliness is half of faith. Vaccines train the body to fight germs. Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria. They do not work on viruses. Only take medicine that a grown-up gives you.

question.hint: They do not work on viruses.
question.explanation: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria.

Germs spread, so wash hands and cover coughs
Only take medicine from a grown-up
